The embedding interface

A host owns the page and its navigation. Lowcoder owns the app rendered inside one element. For communication, build a module and define its inputs, outputs, events and methods in the editor. Their names form your integration contract.

A regular Lowcoder app can also be mounted, but these module APIs do not give the host arbitrary access to its components, queries or internal state.

Host needs to… Use
Load the browser runtime LowcoderSDK.ready
Create or remove an embed mount() · unmount()
Send context into a module setModuleInputs()
Read values or react to an action on()
Run a module’s exposed action invokeMethod()
Render in React LowcoderAppView
Mount with the npm package bootstrapAppAt()
Use existing declarative markup scan()

Use the quickstart for your first embed or jump to the CRM, website, ticketing and POS recipes. This reference covers the complete native embedding interface. Component builders, editor controls, datasource plugin APIs and re-exported utilities in the broader npm package are separate extension APIs.

Choose a distribution

Verified 11 October 2026 The hosted browser SDK and npm package are released separately. This page describes the current hosted SDK, with npm differences called out below.

Capability Hosted browser SDK npm lowcoder-sdk@3.0.0
Entry point https://sdk.lowcoder.cloud/bundle.js import … from "lowcoder-sdk"
Browser facade LowcoderSDK.ready / mount / unmount / scan Not exported; use React or bootstrapAppAt
Instance methods on / setModuleInputs / invokeMethod / destroy on / setModuleInputs / invokeMethod; no destroy
Instance readiness instance.ready; mount awaits definition loading No instance.ready; bootstrap resolves before definition loading finishes
Initial false / 0 / empty string inputs Preserved Can fall back to the module default
React lifecycle fixes Present in current repository source Not yet in the published 3.0.0 package
Import subpath Not applicable lowcoder-sdk/appView points to a missing file in 3.0.0; use the root import

The npm tarball was checked directly against the published 3.0.0 metadata and package contents. Its bundled declarations also omit webUrl and orgId even though the runtime accepts them. Do not infer installed behavior from the repository version number alone.

For the complete lifecycle documented here, use the hosted browser interface. npm users should pin and test their installed version before adopting newer source APIs. The npm build needs a bundler, React and React DOM (declared peers: ≥18), and import 'lowcoder-sdk/dist/style.css'. It is not a standalone script-tag build. Import it only on the client in server-rendered applications.

LowcoderSDK.ready

JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
// sdk.mount, sdk.unmount and sdk.scan are now available.

Promise<LowcoderSDK> · Browser only

Resolves after the initial SDK scripts have loaded and the mount API exists. It does not wait for apps discovered by the automatic markup scan, component rendering or queries.

Rejects if an initial chunk fails to load or initialization does not install the mount API. Catch the promise to show a retry message. A repeated bundle.js tag reuses an existing loader and its promise; it does not reset a failed load. After correcting a network or policy failure, reload the page.

LowcoderSDK.mount()

JavaScript
const sdk = await LowcoderSDK.ready;
const app = await sdk.mount("#customer-panel", {
  appId: "YOUR_PUBLISHED_MODULE_ID",
  moduleInputs: { customerId: "customer-42" }
});

mount(target: string | Element, options: MountOptions): Promise<AppViewInstance>

Parameter Meaning
target An existing DOM element or CSS selector. A selector uses its first match.
options.appId Required application or module ID. Must be non-empty.
options The shared options below, plus appId.

Creates a React root in the element and returns the instance after definition loading and scheduling its render. Calling mount again on an element managed by this facade waits for the previous initialization and destroys its instance before replacing it.

Rejects for a missing/invalid target, invalid selector, missing app ID or an initialization failure. Failed initialization cleans up its root. An initial API 401 instead renders the built-in login prompt and resolves; resolution is not proof of authorization. Later component or query errors are outside this promise.

Give the container dimensions through your host CSS. The SDK has no width, height, timeout or AbortSignal mount options.

LowcoderSDK.unmount()

JavaScript
const container = document.querySelector("#customer-panel");
await LowcoderSDK.unmount(container);
container.remove(); // The host owns removal of the element.

unmount(target: string | Element): Promise<void>

Waits for a mount tracked by this browser facade, destroys the instance and removes its tracking entry. The container stays in the DOM. An unknown or already unmounted element is a no-op. A pending initialization failure can reject this promise; an invalid CSS selector can also reject.

Unmount before removing the element, or keep and pass the element reference. A selector cannot find a detached element. Instances created directly with bootstrapAppAt are not tracked here.

Every initialization option

Option Type / default Behavior
baseUrl string · https://api-service.lowcoder.cloud Lowcoder backend base URL, without a trailing /api. The SDK requests /api/applications/{appId}/view beneath it.
webUrl string · https://app.lowcoder.cloud Lowcoder frontend URL for the authentication flow.
orgId string · omitted Workspace ID used to select the workspace login URL. Does not grant access or set the authenticated identity.
moduleInputs input-name map · omitted Initial values for declared inputs on a root module. See input encoding and updates.
appDsl application definition object · omitted Supply a Lowcoder application DSL instead of fetching the initial definition. The hosted SDK clones it before applying initial inputs.
moduleDslMap map of module ID → DSL · omitted Definitions for nested modules when supplying appDsl. Without appDsl, the server response supplies and replaces this map.

appId is additionally required by browser mount and React, and is the first argument to bootstrapAppAt. Use the actual ID of your published app; the local demo uses a synthetic ID because it supplies its own complete definition.

Supplying appDsl skips the initial app-definition request and JavaScript datasource discovery. It does not promise offline execution: queries, remote components, assets or missing nested definitions may still use the network. Keep DSL compatible with the runtime that loads it.

There are no public token, headers, fetch, theme, onReady or onError initialization options.

JavaScript
const app = await LowcoderSDK.mount("#module", {
  appId: "YOUR_PUBLISHED_MODULE_ID",
  baseUrl: "https://lowcoder.example.com",
  webUrl: "https://lowcoder.example.com",
  orgId: "YOUR_WORKSPACE_ID",
  moduleInputs: { customerId: "customer-42" }
});

instance.ready

JavaScript
await app.ready; // Already fulfilled when hosted sdk.mount() returns.

Promise<void> · Hosted/current source; absent in npm 3.0.0

Waits for initial definition loading (and datasource discovery when applicable), then schedules rendering. It rejects on initial loading failures. It does not wait for a React commit, lazy components, queries or callable module methods.

There is no universal “everything rendered” event. If the host needs business readiness, design a named output or event in the module, such as dataLoaded. That name is your contract, not a built-in SDK event. Event subscriptions do not replay previous values; an early event can be missed. Do not use a one-time startup event as your only readiness guarantee.

instance.setModuleInputs()

JavaScript
app.setModuleInputs({
  customerName: "Ada",          // String input
  quantity: 0,                  // Number input
  enabled: false,               // Boolean input
  customer: JSON.stringify({ id: "customer-42" }), // Data input
  rows: JSON.stringify([{ id: 1, total: 25 }])     // Array input
});

setModuleInputs(inputs: InputMap): void

Updates declared inputs on the mounted root module and schedules rendering. Unknown input names are ignored. Omitted keys and undefined leave existing module values unchanged; this is not a reset or deep merge. Pass a fresh map for each update.

The editor supports Data, String, Array, Number, Boolean and Query input types. Values go through Lowcoder’s code controls: they are source values converted to text, not an arbitrary JavaScript object bridge. Serialize structured Data and Array values with JSON.stringify. Raw objects become [object Object]; arrays are not automatically JSON-encoded.

Plain strings, numbers and booleans work with the corresponding scalar controls. The hosted SDK preserves 0, false and ""; npm 3.0.0 can drop them at initial load. JavaScript null is not a general “clear” operation; for a Data input containing JSON null, pass "null".

Inputs can contain expressions. {{ … }} is interpreted by Lowcoder’s template engine, including inside serialized strings. JSON serialization does not turn this into a guaranteed literal-value channel. Define bounded input contracts and validate untrusted text. Inputs are client-visible context, never authentication or permission checks.

Query inputs represent Lowcoder query bindings. Passing a host function does not create a supported callback bridge. Use module events to request host actions. These update rules also apply to the moduleInputs initialization option and React prop.

instance.on()

JavaScript
let latestOutput;
const stopOutputs = app.on("moduleOutputChange", (output) => {
  latestOutput = output;
  console.log("Current module outputs", output);
});
const stopEvents = app.on("moduleEventTriggered", (eventName) => {
  console.log("Module event", eventName);
});

// When these subscriptions are no longer needed:
stopOutputs();
stopEvents();

on(event, handler?): () => void

Event Handler payload When it fires
moduleOutputChange (output: OutputMap) => void The whole named output object when its values change by deep equality. Not a patch. May initially be empty.
moduleEventTriggered (eventName: string) => void The name of an event explicitly fired by the module. No custom payload or DOM event object.

Each instance has one handler per event type. Registering another replaces the previous one. Fan out within your own handler if several host features need notifications. The returned function removes that subscription; there is no separate off() method.

In the hosted SDK, an old unsubscribe function cannot remove a newer replacement handler. npm 3.0.0 does not have that safeguard. Calling on(event, undefined) returns a no-op function; it does not clear a previous handler.

Subscriptions do not replay a current snapshot. Register immediately after mounting, but do not assume the first output or startup event cannot have occurred already. To exchange results, expose named outputs. There is no atomic event-with-data payload or guaranteed ordering between an event and a separate output update.

Only the two names above are instance events. lowcoder:ready and lowcoder:error belong to the separate browser DOM event interface.

instance.invokeMethod()

JavaScript
// In the Lowcoder editor, define a method named "selectCustomer"
// with parameters in this order: customerId, focusDetails.
// Call after the user can interact with the rendered module.
app.invokeMethod("selectCustomer", ["customer-42", true]);

invokeMethod(methodName: string, params: any[] = []): void

Runs an action exposed as a named module method. Arguments are positional, in the order configured in the editor. A missing, undefined or null argument uses that parameter’s default; 0, false and "" are retained. Extra arguments are ignored.

The name must identify a configured module method, not an arbitrary component function or query. An unknown method, a normal app instead of a module, or a call before the module root exists silently does nothing. Calls are not queued.

No return-value promise. The SDK discards the internal action result. await app.invokeMethod(...) does not wait for the action to finish and does not catch its asynchronous errors. Model completion, results and failures as module outputs/events.

Use a request ID in your module contract when correlating asynchronous work with host actions. For actions such as saving, submitting or charging, perform authoritative validation and state changes on your backend.

instance.destroy()

JavaScript
app.destroy(); // Synchronous; safe to call more than once.

destroy(): void · Hosted/current source; absent in npm 3.0.0

Clears instance handlers, releases the module reference and unmounts its React root. It leaves the host element in place. Further input updates and method calls have no effect.

It does not cancel outstanding HTTP requests or undo shared SDK configuration, global CSS or page-level state. For instances owned by the browser facade, prefer await LowcoderSDK.unmount(container), which also clears that facade’s tracking entry. Do not manually destroy an instance owned by a React wrapper that is managing its lifecycle.

Instance & TypeScript types

AppViewInstance<I, O> represents an embedded app. I describes its input-name map and O its output object. Keep the instance returned by a factory; do not construct a second React root on an element already owned by an embed.

The runtime class constructor is new AppViewInstance(appId, node, root, options = {}), where root is a React DOM Root. It is a low-level implementation surface: use bootstrapAppAt or browser mount so component registration, root creation and initialization cleanup happen together.

  • AppViewInstanceOptions<I>: the six initialization options, with moduleInputs?: I.
  • LowcoderAppViewProps<I, O>: those options plus appId, className and the two callbacks.
  • OutputChangeHandler<O> = (output: O) => void.
  • EventTriggerHandler = (eventName: string) => void.

InputMap, OutputMap and MountOptions in this reference describe the shapes of values; they are not named npm exports. Generic types do not validate values at runtime. The browser facade is a script global, not an npm export. Published npm 3.0.0 has incomplete declaration routing as well as the missing members listed in the distribution table; verify your toolchain instead of assuming current source declarations are installed.

bootstrapAppAt()

JavaScript
import { bootstrapAppAt } from "lowcoder-sdk";
import "lowcoder-sdk/dist/style.css";

const app = await bootstrapAppAt(
  "YOUR_PUBLISHED_MODULE_ID",
  document.getElementById("customer-panel"),
  { moduleInputs: { customerId: "customer-42" } }
);

bootstrapAppAt(appId: string, node: Element, options = {}): Promise<AppViewInstance>

The low-level imperative factory exported by the npm package. Unlike browser mount, it requires an element, not a selector. Supply the same initialization options, with appId as the first argument. The browser bundle also exposes the broader exports through window.$lowcoder_sdk; prefer LowcoderSDK.mount for browser integrations.

In current source, the factory checks for a node, waits for instance.ready, and cleans up on initialization failure. It does not track or replace an existing root on that element. The published npm 3.0.0 factory returns before definition loading finishes, and its instance has neither ready nor destroy. Its declaration requires the options argument, so pass {} when using defaults. Use the hosted facade for screens requiring the documented cleanup lifecycle until an npm release includes those fixes.

LowcoderAppView

React / JSX
import { useMemo } from "react";
import { LowcoderAppView } from "lowcoder-sdk";
import "lowcoder-sdk/dist/style.css";

export function CustomerPanel({ customerId }) {
  const inputs = useMemo(() => ({ customerId }), [customerId]);
  return (
    <div style={{ minHeight: 360 }}>
      <LowcoderAppView
        appId="YOUR_PUBLISHED_MODULE_ID"
        className="customer-module"
        moduleInputs={inputs}
        onModuleOutputChange={(output) => console.log(output)}
        onModuleEventTriggered={(name) => console.log(name)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
Prop Meaning
appId Required string: the published application or module ID.
All six initialization options baseUrl, webUrl, orgId, moduleInputs, appDsl, moduleDslMap.
className Optional string on the wrapper element. Set size through a host wrapper or CSS.
onModuleOutputChange Optional (output) => void; same payload as the instance output event.
onModuleEventTriggered Optional (eventName: string) => void.
ref Forwarded instance reference; initially undefined. Not a guarantee that all components or queries have finished.

Lifecycle in current source

Changes to appId, baseUrl, webUrl or orgId recreate the instance. A new moduleInputs object updates inputs; callback prop changes replace subscriptions. Changes to appDsl or moduleDslMap alone do not reload the app: change the React key when replacing a supplied definition. Cleanup disposes the owned instance.

These lifecycle fixes are not in npm 3.0.0. Do not rely on cleanup or backend switching described above in that published version. The npm React wrapper also does not provide the new instance readiness/disposal API.

Arbitrary HTML props such as style and id are not forwarded; put them on your host wrapper. There is no public onError prop. The current wrapper logs initial mount failures to the console. Use the hosted imperative API if the host needs to own loading, failure and retry UI.

The wrapper uses the same single event-handler slots as instance.on. Registering a second handler through the ref can replace the corresponding callback prop subscription.

LowcoderSDK.scan()

JavaScript
await LowcoderSDK.ready;
await LowcoderSDK.scan(document.getElementById("new-widgets"));

scan(root: ParentNode = document): Promise<void[]>

Finds descendant .lowcoder-module-container elements and mounts their display elements. The root itself is not included. The browser entry scans the document automatically at DOM readiness. Call this again for markup inserted later.

Skips containers without a display element and display elements already tracked by the facade. It returns an array of undefined results, not app instances. Individual JSON or mount errors are caught and emitted on the affected container as lowcoder:error; the scan can resolve even if an embed failed. An invalid root can reject.

Listen directly to each container for its events. Use explicit mount when you need an instance, individual failure handling or lifecycle control.

Declarative HTML contract

HTML
<div class="lowcoder-module-container" id="customer-widget">
  <input type="hidden" class="module-id" value="YOUR_PUBLISHED_MODULE_ID">
  <input type="hidden" class="module-input" value='{"customerId":"customer-42"}'>
  <input type="hidden" class="locoder-backend-url" value="https://api-service.lowcoder.cloud">
  <input type="hidden" class="locoder-frontend-url" value="https://app.lowcoder.cloud">
  <input type="hidden" class="locoder-org-id" value="YOUR_WORKSPACE_ID">
  <div class="lowcoder-module-display"></div>
</div>
<script src="https://sdk.lowcoder.cloud/bundle.js"></script>
Class Meaning
lowcoder-module-container Parent container found by the scanner.
lowcoder-module-display Descendant DOM element where the app is mounted.
module-id Input whose value is the required app ID.
module-input Input containing a JSON object of module inputs; defaults to {}.
locoder-backend-url Optional backend URL; same default as baseUrl.
locoder-frontend-url Optional frontend URL; same default as webUrl.
locoder-org-id Optional workspace login ID.

The historical spelling locoder-… is required. Changing a hidden field after mounting does not update that instance; the scanner skips existing mounts. Unmount its display element before scanning again, or use explicit mount and setModuleInputs.

The scanner also calls optional globals window.opChange(output) and window.onModuleEventTriggered(eventName). They are shared across all scanned embeds and carry no instance identity. Prefer listeners on the individual container. A throwing global callback can interrupt subsequent container event delivery.

Browser DOM events

Event target Name event.detail
window lowcoder:ready No payload. Initial browser runtime loaded.
window lowcoder:error Error from initial loader failure; not a catch-all runtime error event.
Scanned container lowcoder:output Whole module output object.
Scanned container lowcoder:event Module event name string.
Scanned container lowcoder:error Error parsing its JSON or mounting its app.
JavaScript
const container = document.getElementById("customer-widget");
container.addEventListener("lowcoder:output", (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail);
});
container.addEventListener("lowcoder:error", (event) => {
  console.error("This embed failed", event.detail);
});

These CustomEvents do not bubble. Register on the stated target before the event can fire. Explicit mount() does not emit the scanner’s container events; subscribe on its returned instance instead. Prefer the ready promise to a window readiness listener that could be attached too late.

Authentication & deployment boundaries

The initial app request uses credentials/cookies. An initial 401 displays a built-in login prompt. Login opens {webUrl}/user/auth/login, or {webUrl}/org/{orgId}/auth/login when a workspace is supplied. The prompt’s Refresh action reloads the entire host page. Other initial failures, including 403, reject hosted mounting.

Configure backend CORS and cookie settings for the actual host origin, and test the browser’s cross-site cookie behavior. CORS on the SDK’s static files does not grant access to the Lowcoder API. There is no public bearer-token option, request-header hook, logout method or automatic transfer of your host’s SSO session.

Multiple embeds can coexist, but the runtime shares configuration, Redux state, history and CSS. Use one Lowcoder deployment per page. Passing a different backend to each instance does not provide independent isolation. Native DOM integration is not a Shadow DOM or CSS sandbox; test host styles, overlays and routing.

To self-host, serve bundle.js with its complete emitted asset directory. The loader resolves chunks relative to its own URL. Retain old hashed assets during upgrades so already open pages can still load their lazy chunks. The loader propagates its script nonce to initial scripts; this is not a guarantee that the full runtime supports your strict CSP.

Troubleshooting by symptom

Symptom What to check
The page stays blank Catch LowcoderSDK.ready and mount() errors. Check chunk requests, backend access, container size and runtime console errors.
Inputs appear unchanged Embed a module; declare the exact input names and types. Send a fresh map. Serialize Data/Array values. Omitted keys do not reset values.
A method does nothing Use a declared module method, wait for the rendered module to be usable, and match parameter order. Mount readiness alone is insufficient.
An awaited method finishes instantly invokeMethod returns void. Expose completion through your module contract.
A listener stops firing There is one handler per event. Another registration or a React callback prop may have replaced it.
An initial output was missed Subscriptions have no replay. Avoid depending on a single startup emission for a handshake.
A private embed shows Login Mount can resolve to the auth prompt. Verify cookies, allowed origins, publication/access settings and frontend login URL.
destroy / ready / appView import is missing Check the distribution table; npm 3.0.0 is not equivalent to the hosted bundle.
Host styles or another embed change Configuration, routing and CSS are shared. Keep the same deployment across embeds and check host integration boundaries.

This reference is derived from the browser facade, loader, AppViewInstance, bootstrap factory, React wrapper and module input/method implementations in the Lowcoder client source. The distribution notes record the separately inspected npm artifact. Repository changes and published artifacts can differ; the version table makes that distinction explicit.
